column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the truthful one, the one believed, narrated to us: “The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clinging clot for a like period, then a lump of flesh for a like period. Then the angel is sent to him,
breathes the soul into him, and is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy.

By Allah, besides whom there is no god, one of you will do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a forearm's length between him and it, then what is written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it.

And one of you will do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a forearm's length between him and it, then what is written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Al-ṣādiq (“the truthful one”): the one who informs of the truth. Al-maṣdūq (“the one believed”): Allah has been true to him in His promise. Yujmaʿu khalquhu (“his creation is gathered”): after being dispersed in the womb, from the woman's fluid and the man's semen. Fī baṭni ummihi (“in his mother's womb”):

in her uterus. Nuṭfah (“a drop”): semen. ʿAlaqah (“a clinging clot”): a piece of blood. Muḍghah (“a lump of flesh”): a piece of flesh the size of a mouthful that is chewed. Mithla dhālik (“for a like period”): of time, namely forty days.

Yursalu ilayhi al-malak (“the angel is sent to him”): the angel entrusted with the womb. Yaktubu rizqahu (“to write down his provision”): its measure, little or much. Wa-ajalahu (“and his lifespan”): the end of his life. “Do the deeds of the people of Paradise”: acts of obedience.

“Do the deeds of the people of the Fire”: acts of disobedience. Ḥattā makes the verb subjunctive and mā is negative; it is also permissible to put yakūnu in the indicative, with ḥattā introducing a new clause. Yasbiqu ʿalayhi al-kitāb (“what is written overtakes him”): the writing in which his fate is recorded.
An indication of knowledge of the beginning and the return, and an explanation of what relates to the human being and his state of wretchedness or happiness, poverty or wealth.
The permissibility of swearing an oath on a true report to make it firm in the listener's mind.
Belief in the resurrection and the raising up after death.
Affirming the decree and believing in it.
Contentment with the provision Allah has decreed for His servant, and avoiding intense greed since provision is decreed, while still taking the means.
Fear of a bad ending.
Repentance demolishes what came before it.
Happiness and wretchedness have already been written, and everyone is eased towards what he was created for.

This hadith explains the beginning of the human being in his mother's womb and his moving from one stage to another, from semen to a clinging clot to a lump of flesh, formed and unformed. Then the angel is sent to him and breathes the soul into him,

which flows through his body, and he begins to move. The angel writes down the provision he will have in this world, little or much, until he dies; he writes the measure of his life and its end, and what he will do of good, evil and the permissible, and his happiness or wretchedness.
Then the Messenger ﷺ made clear that the human being's outcome is either Paradise or the Fire,
and he ﷺ gave an example to warn against a bad ending. Its meaning is that among the children of Ādam is one who spends his whole life in obedience to Allah,

then, when the time comes for his soul to be taken, he associates partners with Allah or disbelieves and dies, and so he is among the people of the Fire; and another who spent his whole life in disbelief and sin, but as his appointed time drew near he accepted Islam, repented and turned back to Allah the Exalted,
then died and became one of the people of Paradise. So every Muslim should fear a bad ending. We ask Allah for a good ending.
Know, by Allah, that you will receive all that / is inscribed and written for you in the Book.
No man's provision was ever increased / by eagerness, nor diminished by falling short.
The believer must take the means. The poet said, drawing on the meaning of the Noble Qurʾān:
Do you not see that Allah said to Maryam, / “Shake the trunk towards you; it will let fall fresh dates”?
Had He willed, He would have brought the trunk near to her without her shaking it, / but everything has its means.
The believer must be content with what Allah the Exalted has decreed. The poet said:
I have nothing but contentment with what Allah has decreed, / whether I loved it or disliked it.
Even if I strove with all my effort / to ward off a decreed matter, I would not ward it off.
So I see fit to refer that to the One / who has knowledge of all that I do not know.
